sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell a house in South Brunswick?
sections.html:
A South Brunswick owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept an as-is offer from a buyer who pays cash. All three routes meet the same township step: a Residential Resale Certificate of Occupancy, which the Planning office issues before the deed changes hands.

Listing reaches the most buyers in a township where the median owner-occupied home is valued at $582,700, but it adds commissions, showings and a township inspection that you schedule around the sale. A direct sale gives up some price for speed and usually skips repair negotiations. Whichever you choose, sort out the permit history first, because the township will not issue the resale certificate while any permit or inspection is still open.

sections.h2: Where is South Brunswick and which villages does it include?
sections.html:
South Brunswick is a Middlesex County township of 41.02 square miles, 40.61 of them land, in the middle of the Raritan Valley. It borders Cranbury, East Brunswick, Monroe, North Brunswick and Plainsboro in Middlesex County, Princeton in Mercer County and Franklin Township in Somerset County. The Lawrence Brook runs through the center of the township, and Pigeon Swamp State Park holds 1,078 acres of undeveloped land off Deans Rhode Hall Road.

There is no single downtown. Instead the township is a set of unincorporated villages, each with its own mail address, and buyers often search by village name. Several ZIP codes share the township, including 08810 for Dayton, 08824 for Kendall Park, 08852 for Monmouth Junction and 08528 for Kingston, so a listing should name the village clearly. The 2020 Census counted these communities:

  • Kendall Park: 9,989 residents
  • Monmouth Junction: 8,895
  • Dayton: 8,138
  • Heathcote: 7,154
  • Deans: 1,615
  • Kingston: 1,581

sections.h2: How did South Brunswick grow, and what does that mean for the houses?
sections.html:
The township was incorporated on February 21, 1798, and farmed for most of its first two centuries. The Straight Turnpike, now Route 1, opened in 1804, a trolley line followed in 1900, and the New Jersey Turnpike arrived in 1951. Suburban building began after World War II, and Kendall Park was started in 1957 off Route 27, an old Native American trail.

The population was close to 18,000 in 1980, reached 25,792 in 1990 and stood at 47,043 in 2020, the highest decennial count on record. Because so much of that growth came after 1980, many homes are old enough that a furnace, water heater or central air unit has been replaced at least once. The township resale form asks about each of those replacements, so keep invoices and permit numbers together before you apply. Warehouses now fill much of the land between Route 130 and the Turnpike on the southeast side.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about South Brunswick homeowners?
sections.html:
QuickFacts estimates 47,454 residents for July 2025, up 0.9% from the April 2020 base. Of the 16,770 households counted for 2020 to 2024, 76.9% own their home, and the average household has 2.81 people. Median household income is $150,933, median gross rent is $1,935, and 68.9% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

About 42.2% of residents were born outside the United States and 52.7% of people age 5 and over speak a language other than English at home. Sellers who advertise in more than one language, or who share a floor plan and inspection summary with buyers ahead of a tour, tend to avoid repeat questions. Workers travel 34.4 minutes on average to their jobs, which matches the township's role as an outer-ring New York suburb. Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts.

sections.h2: What does the South Brunswick resale certificate cover?
sections.html:
The Residential Resale Certificate of Occupancy, under section 22-425 of the township code, is a general inspection of the visible parts of the dwelling. The application says it confirms three things: no work was done that needed a construction or zoning permit, no permits or inspections remain outstanding, and no visible violations or unsafe conditions exist. If an inspector finds a problem, you must obtain the missing permits and satisfy the inspections before the certificate is released.

sections.h2: Which past projects should I check before booking the inspection?
sections.html:
The application asks whether the home has had any of the following, and for the permit number if so. Anything done without a permit has to be permitted and inspected before the certificate can issue, even if a previous owner did the work.

  • Replacement central air conditioning, furnace or water heater
  • Generator or radon system
  • Addition or finished basement
  • Fireplace or wood stove
  • Shed larger than 200 square feet
  • Swimming pool, hot tub, deck or gazebo

The Building Department administers the state Uniform Construction Code and handles permits, but it does not process resale certificates. Direct resale questions to the Zoning office. Any permits and certificates of approval that come out of the process are passed to the Tax Assessor, so the new work will appear on the property record.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and bus lines do South Brunswick buyers ask about?
sections.html:
South Brunswick Public Schools serves pre-kindergarten through grade 12 with 12 schools and 7,936 students in 2023-24, down from 8,620 in 2018-19. The elementary schools are Brooks Crossing, Brunswick Acres, Cambridge, Constable, Greenbrook, Indian Fields and Monmouth Junction, with Dayton and Deans preschools. Crossroads Middle School North and South serve grades 6 to 8, and South Brunswick High School has 2,728 students.

A 3.5-mile stretch of the New Jersey Turnpike crosses the east side, with the toll gate for Exit 8A just over the line in Monroe. U.S. 1, U.S. 130, Route 27 and Route 32 cross the township, along with county routes 535 and 522. A park and ride near Routes 32 and 130 offers Suburban Transit lines 300 (Port Authority, Grand Central and the East Side) and 600 (Downtown Manhattan). The Middlesex County Area Transit shuttle links to NJ Transit, and the nearest train stations are at Princeton Junction and New Brunswick.

Large employers in the township include Dow Jones, International Flavors and Fragrances, L'Oreal, Canon, UPS, Tris Pharma and the school district itself, which gives many buyers a job base inside the township.

sections.h2: What state paperwork comes with a South Brunswick closing?
sections.html:
New Jersey puts the Realty Transfer Fee on the seller, collected when the deed is recorded and scaled to the price stated in the deed. A deed that claims an exemption, such as a transfer between spouses or between parent and child, needs Form RTF-1. For Class 2 residential sales above $1,000,000, a supplemental graduated fee starts at 1% of the total price.

The seller also signs a Gross Income Tax residency form, GIT/REP-3 for New Jersey residents. A nonresident seller prepays at least 2% of the total consideration unless a stated exception applies. Both sets of rules are on the Division of Taxation realty transfer fee page and its GIT/REP FAQ. Your closing attorney or title agent will prepare the forms.

sections.h2: Does the Kingston historic district affect a sale?
sections.html: The Kingston Mill Historic District covers 49 acres around the village of Kingston, which sits where South Brunswick meets Princeton and Franklin Township. It joined the National Register of Historic Places on April 10, 1986, and includes the 1888 Kingston Mill and the 1798 Kingston Bridge. Owners of older Kingston houses should ask the township Planning office whether an address lies inside the district before they plan exterior changes ahead of a sale.

faqs.q: Do I need a township inspection to sell a house in South Brunswick?
faqs.a: Yes. South Brunswick requires a Residential Resale Certificate of Occupancy under section 22-425 of the township code. The inspection looks at visible components and checks for unpermitted work, open permits and unsafe conditions.

faqs.q: How long does the South Brunswick resale certificate last?
faqs.a: It is effective for 120 days, and the inspecting officer may grant one extension of up to 30 days. If the house has not sold by then and is still on the market, the owner must apply again and obtain a new certificate.

faqs.q: Which township office handles resale certificates?
faqs.a: The Zoning office does, at 732-329-4000 ext. 7240. The Building Department says it handles construction permits and new construction certificates, and sends resale questions to Zoning.

faqs.q: Can I sell with work that was done without a permit?
faqs.a: The township wants the permits and inspections satisfied before it issues the resale certificate, so unpermitted work has to be brought into compliance first. Ask your attorney how the sale contract should address any cost of doing so.

faqs.q: Who pays the New Jersey realty transfer fee in South Brunswick?
faqs.a: The seller does. The state collects it when the deed is recorded, and the rate rises with the price in the deed. Sales above $1,000,000 also carry the graduated percent fee, starting at 1%.
